workflow: An isolated execution context is created with a copied configuration containing owned dynamic data.
The context is later destroyed, but teardown releases ordinary state without clearing the copied configuration data.
Repeated creation and destruction leaves those configuration allocations unreachable but unreclaimed.
Leak detection reports persistent memory growth and marks the otherwise successful operation as failed.
summary: Per-context configuration storage leaks across repeated teardown cycles
decision_reason: The bug is materially the same as repeated isolated-context teardown leaking context-owned auxiliary storage; only the omitted storage category differs.
